Hi Dear Chalmers,
After three years of interval, I have another few questions about Mirt.
(also thank you for your advices in the past. they helped me to structure my dissertation, and it finished)

My question is about comparison of fit indices obtained from mirt package and lavaan package (or MPULUS).
Spesifically, I want to see comparison of lavaan results(with MLE estimation) and mirt results (grm, grsm, gpcm and  unfolding model). Which fit indices serve to this aim (AIC, BIC, RMSEA, CFI, TLI, G2...?)

Also, I get the parameters for this study for all the methods mentioned above  (for three dimensional structure data).
I realized that unfolding model item loadings are negatively correlated with all the other methods (even with efa). What could be the reason?
Not: Basically I use the following code:
library(mirt)
cmodel <- mirt.model('
F1 = 1,2,3,4,5,6
F2 = 7,8,9,10,11,12
F3 = 13,14,15,16,17,18
COV=F1*F2*F3')
cmodggum <- mirt(data, cmodel, itemtype = 'ggum')

On Mon, Mar 26, 2018 at 3:10 AM, Kiff Cu <avcu...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Dear Chalmers,
After three years of interval, I have another few questions about Mirt.
(also thank you for your advices in the past. they helped me to structure my dissertation, and it finished)

My question is about comparison of fit indices obtained from mirt package and lavaan package (or MPULUS).
Spesifically, I want to see comparison of lavaan results(with MLE estimation)

lavaan can estimate categorical responses with MLE? That seems less likely to me, it is much more known for WLSMV estimator. If it does do MLE (it might, I've never tested it) then I can't imagine it does so very efficiently without compiled code.....
and mirt results (grm, grsm, gpcm and  unfolding model). Which fit indices serve to this aim (AIC, BIC, RMSEA, CFI, TLI, G2...?)

If what you're referring to is really the WLSMV estimator then any information/log-likelihood based criteria would be out (AIC, BIC, ect). The M2() function would give you similar residual covariance information though, as well as associated CFI and TLI stats.

Also, I get the parameters for this study for all the methods mentioned above  (for three dimensional structure data).
I realized that unfolding model item loadings are negatively correlated with all the other methods (even with efa). What could be the reason?
Not: Basically I use the following code:
library(mirt)
cmodel <- mirt.model('
F1 = 1,2,3,4,5,6
F2 = 7,8,9,10,11,12
F3 = 13,14,15,16,17,18
COV=F1*F2*F3')
cmodggum <- mirt(data, cmodel, itemtype = 'ggum')

Ideal point models like ggum are not related to the cumulative models that are commonly found in IRT and SEM. So they don't have the same properties or interpretations.
